office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Brad Barrett
incumbent.summary: Brad Barrett, a retired Richmond general surgeon, has represented House District 56 since 2018 and chairs the House Public Health Committee [3]. He announced in January 2026 that he would not seek reelection, giving no specific reason; his term ends in November [4].
record: Committees: Public Health (chair), Agriculture and Rural Development, and Insurance [3]. First elected in 2018 after defeating incumbent Rep. Richard Hamm in the Republican primary [4].

2024: Authored HEA 1385, requiring insurers to reimburse out-of-network ambulance services and pay claims within 30 days [5]. 2025: Sponsored SB 2 on Medicaid oversight and fraud reporting, which passed both chambers [6]. 2026: Authored HB 1277 on Medicaid assisted-living services, which passed the House [7].

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) [8]; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) [9]; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) [10].
On leaving, said: "Serving the people of Wayne and Henry counties has been one of the greatest honors of my life" [4].

race_context: House District 56 covers all of Wayne County, including Richmond, and part of Henry County [3].
Open seat: Rep. Brad Barrett announced on Jan. 7, 2026 that he would not seek a fifth term [4]. Barrett was reelected unopposed in 2024 [11].

May 5, 2026 Republican primary: Randy Retter 3,250 votes (53.0%), Pete Zaleski 2,603 (42.4%), Adam Blanton 281 (4.6%) [11]. Blanton, an assistant Richmond police chief, withdrew in March and endorsed Zaleski, but stayed on the ballot [12]. Rockwell was the only Democrat to file [13, 11].

Key differences: Retter emphasizes public safety, school security and law-enforcement links to addiction treatment [14]; Rockwell emphasizes worker protections, public-school funding, universal health coverage and ending partisan gerrymandering [15].
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Randy Retter is the two-term Wayne County sheriff, who is term-limited in that office [13]. He won a three-way Republican primary with 53% of the vote [11].
background: Began his law enforcement career in 1988 and was elected Wayne County sheriff in 2018; now in his second term [16]. Cannot run for sheriff again because of term limits [13].
Bachelor's degree in criminal justice from Ball State University and graduate of the Indiana Law Enforcement Academy [13].
Serves on the Boys & Girls Club board [17]; lives in Wayne County across from his family farm [16].
path_to_ballot: Announced Jan. 9, 2026 [16]; won the May 5 Republican primary over Pete Zaleski and Adam Blanton with 53.0% [11].

items: Says he would make school safety protocols a priority, support first responders and use data to reduce repeat offenses [14].
Says he supports lowering health care costs and protecting rural access to care, building on Barrett's work [14].
Says he has worked to expand partnerships for mental health and addiction treatment and wants to connect law enforcement and health care [14].
Says he would reduce regulation on small businesses and family farms and bring jobs to eastern Indiana [14].
Says he would apply the budget discipline of the sheriff's office to state government and seek a fair share of infrastructure funding for rural areas [14].

on_incumbent: His campaign describes his health-care plans as building on "the work of Dr. Brad Barrett" [14]. At his announcement he said: "After many years in public service, I've seen firsthand the challenges and opportunities facing our rural communities" [16].
plans: Says he wants "strong, steady leadership that puts Hoosiers first and reflects the values of the people who live and work here" [13].
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: Wikipedia lists an NRA Political Victory Fund endorsement; not verified on the NRA site.
The Palladium-Item's Jan. 15, 2026 article on his launch could not be fetched.

candidates.summary: Tom Rockwell is a Richmond Quaker minister and pastor running as the Democratic nominee [13, 15]. His platform focuses on wages and worker rights, public schools, health care, rural investment and election reform [15].
background: Pastor of a small rural church and a denominational leader; has also run a small forestry business working with farmers and landowners [13].
Earned a Master of Divinity from the Earlham School of Religion in 2024 and works at Western Yearly Meeting; he and his wife co-pastor a Quaker church [18].
Age 34; has lived in Richmond for six years [15].
path_to_ballot: Filed Feb. 3, 2026 [13]; the only Democrat in the May 5 primary [11].

items: Supports collective bargaining, a higher minimum wage, action on wage theft, apprenticeships, and tenant protections [15].
Supports protecting workers from AI-related job loss and surveillance and requiring transparency when AI is used in major public systems [15].
Supports fully funding public schools, raising teacher pay and expanding vocational and community-college options [15].
Supports universal coverage, preventive and maternal care, and mental health and addiction services [15]; has cited affordable, accessible health care as a rural concern [13].
Supports funding first responders, mental-health crisis response, addiction treatment and domestic-violence services [15].
Supports campaign-finance transparency, ending partisan gerrymandering, public town halls and local control over schools, libraries and public safety [15].
Supports downtown revitalization, support for manufacturers and family farms, rural health care and infrastructure repair [15].

on_incumbent: On the district's direction, said: "Too often, the proposed solutions for communities like ours focus on attracting outside companies" and "I believe the real expertise already lives here" [13]. No statements about Retter were found.
plans: His campaign says he would hold public town halls and Zoom sessions [15].
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement from the Indiana Reproductive Freedom PAC [19].
gaps: Little news coverage beyond his filing was found.
He did not answer the iVoterGuide questionnaire.
